examples.name: Default
examples.summary: A ProductWidget console screen in the framed panel with three tabs; the scene slot receives the selected tab and shows that widget. The bottom fifth is cropped and faded from the medium breakpoint up.
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import ConsolePanel from '@aziontech/webkit/console-panel'
  import ProductWidget from '@aziontech/webkit/product-widget'

  const tabs = [
    { value: 'workloads-list', title: 'Workloads' },
    { value: 'workload-deployments', title: 'Deployments' },
    { value: 'workload-deploy-logs', title: 'Logs' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <ConsolePanel
    eyebrow="Console"
    title="One console for every workload"
    description="Deploy, observe and secure from the same place."
    :tabs="tabs"
    :crop="0.2"
  >
    <template #scene="{ tab }">
      <ProductWidget :name="tab ?? 'workloads-list'" />
    </template>
  </ConsolePanel>
</template>

examples.name: Diagram
examples.summary: `variant="diagram"` lets the scene keep its own height, centered on the texture, with an action under the title instead of tabs.
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import ConsolePanel from '@aziontech/webkit/console-panel'
  import Illustration from '@aziontech/webkit/illustration'
</script>

<template>
  <ConsolePanel
    variant="diagram"
    title="Requests take the shortest path"
    :primary-action="{ label: 'See the network', href: '/network', trailing: true }"
  >
    <template #scene>
      <Illustration
        name="global-network"
        aria-label="Requests routed to the nearest location"
        class="max-w-(--container-lg)"
      />
    </template>
  </ConsolePanel>
</template>
